title: Great GASPI Data Schema
perspective: Uyghur Rights Preservation / World Uyghur Congress / Diaspora Archives

control_zones.zone_name: Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (Bingtuan) Occupied Lands
control_zones.access_restrictions: Bingtuan-controlled areas are heavily monitored; access restricted for Uyghur populations; mandatory surveillance and movement controls
strategic_features_located_here: Border regions with strategic military presence

control_zones.governing_authority: Local Party Committees / Public Security Bureau
control_zones.access_restrictions: Checkpoints every 100 yards in cities like Kashgar; residents require permits to leave registered areas; movement severely restricted [citation:9][citation:12]

control_zones.zone_name: Vocational Education and Training Centers (VETCs) / Detention Facilities
control_zones.access_restrictions: Highly restricted; detainees held without due process; released individuals subject to ongoing surveillance [citation:4][citation:12]
strategic_features_located_here: Re-education camps (terminology disputed by Chinese authorities)
Industrial parks with forced labor facilities

demographics.notes: Chinese state statistics report Uyghur population growth: 8.3456 million in 2000, 10.0013 million in 2010, and 11.6243 million in 2020 [citation:2]. However, diaspora and rights organizations dispute these figures, citing forced birth control, sterilization, and demographic engineering. The Uyghur population is concentrated in southern Xinjiang (Kashgar, Hotan, Aksu, Kizilsu), where they constitute 83.74% of the population . Estimates of detention range from 900,000 to 1.5 million people, based on leaked data sets [citation:4].
demographics.citation: Xinjiang 2025 National Economic and Social Development Statistical Bulletin; The Intercept data leak

named_high_ground_features.name: Tian Shan Mountains
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Natural barrier separating northern and southern Xinjiang; controls movement corridors and observation points over major population centers

named_high_ground_features.name: Tarim Basin (Southern Xinjiang)
named_high_ground_features.functional_strategic_description: Primary Uyghur-populated region; location of major cotton production and water resources; controlled through surveillance and checkpoints [citation:11]

physical_barriers.name: Checkpoint Network and Surveillance Infrastructure
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Massive expansion post-2014; checkpoints every 100 yards in cities like Kashgar; grid-management system implemented [citation:9][citation:12]
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Chinese authorities claim checkpoints are counter-terrorism measures to combat the 'three forces' of separatism, extremism, and terrorism [citation:5][citation:13]
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Uyghur rights organizations characterize the checkpoint network as a system of collective punishment and racial profiling that restricts movement, separates families, and creates a 'normalization of fear' [citation:4][citation:9]
physical_barriers.citation: Human Rights Watch; The Intercept; RNA Media

physical_barriers.name: Vocational Education and Training Centers (VETCs)
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Established 2017; phased transformation to 'vocational schools' but detention continues; many trainees still unaccounted for [citation:4]
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Chinese authorities describe VETCs as schools for deradicalization, similar to programs in the UK and France; trainees learn language, law, and vocational skills [citation:1][citation:6][citation:13]
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Uyghur rights organizations characterize VETCs as high-tech penal colonies with forced labor, surveillance, and cultural assimilation; estimate 900,000 to 1.5 million people have been detained [citation:4][citation:12]
physical_barriers.citation: Human Rights Watch; Darren Byler interview; China Law Translate

water_infrastructure.name: Tarim River Basin
water_infrastructure.controlling_entity: Chinese government / Tarim River Basin Water Resource Commission
water_infrastructure.capacity_or_flow_rate: China's largest inland river; critical for irrigated agriculture including cotton production; experiences severe water scarcity and resource competition [citation:11]

agriculture.notes: Xinjiang leads in cotton production in China; Bingtuan controls 30% of stable land with only 12% of population [citation:11]. Cotton production relies on intensive irrigation from the Tarim River, causing resource competition and salinization. Uyghur farmers face restrictions on water use compared to state farms [citation:11]

environmental_degradation_incidents.incident_type: Soil salinization and water resource depletion
environmental_degradation_incidents.stated_justification: Chinese authorities implement subsurface drainage and irrigation technologies to combat salinization [citation:8][citation:15]
environmental_degradation_incidents.opposing_characterization: Uyghur and environmental groups characterize cotton production as exacerbating water scarcity and damaging the fragile ecosystem of the Tarim Basin

airspace_and_spectrum.cellular_tech_allowed: 3G, 4G, 5G with heavy surveillance; internet and messaging apps monitored [citation:9]
airspace_and_spectrum.flight_corridor_control: Airspace controlled by Chinese authorities; military presence at airports
airspace_and_spectrum.opposing_characterization: Digital surveillance and control of communications are used to monitor and suppress Uyghur communities

controlled_item_categories: Cotton and textiles (subject to international sanctions and forced labor allegations)
Oil and gas (extracted in Xinjiang and transferred to inland provinces)
trade_and_dual_use_controls.transit_permit_regimes: Movement between cities requires permits and identity checks; Uyghurs face stricter controls
trade_and_dual_use_controls.opposing_characterization: Resource extraction disproportionately benefits Han Chinese and the state; oil, cotton, and other resources are transferred out of Xinjiang

checkpoints_and_gates.name: Kashgar City Checkpoints
checkpoints_and_gates.permit_type_required: Identity card verification; biometric scanning; travel permits to leave areas
checkpoints_and_gates.opposing_characterization: Uyghurs require permits to leave their registered areas; checkpoints are used to monitor and control movement [citation:9][citation:12]

checkpoints_and_gates.name: Integrated Joint Operations Platform (IJOP) Checkpoints
checkpoints_and_gates.permit_type_required: Digital identity verification; biometric data check
checkpoints_and_gates.opposing_characterization: IJOP system collects massive personal data (fingerprints, iris scans, DNA, voice samples) and flags 'suspicious' behavior, triggering investigations and detention [citation:4][citation:12]

power_generating_assets: Coal and hydroelectric plants in Xinjiang
Tarim Basin oil and gas extraction sites
utilities_and_energy_grid.debt_or_fiscal_transfer_mechanisms: Resource extraction revenue largely flows to central government and inland provinces

jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.enforced_system_name: Chinese National Law / Counter-Terrorism Law / De-extremification Regulations
jurisprudence_and_statutory_friction.preferred_or_prior_system_name: Uyghur customary law / Islamic law / UN human rights standards
enforced_statutes_cited: Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region Regulations on De-extremification
Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region Measures on the Implementation of the Counter-Terrorism Law

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.case_or_resolution_name: OHCHR Report on Human Rights in Xinjiang
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights found significant concerns about arbitrary detention, torture, forced labor, and restrictions on fundamental freedoms in Xinjiang
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: Chinese authorities reject the report, claiming it is based on fabricated evidence and biased sources

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Declared China's actions in Xinjiang a 'massive human rights abuse' and imposed sanctions on officials and entities
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: Chinese government denounces the act as interference in internal affairs and rejects its findings

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: XUAR De-extremification Regulations (identifies 15 manifestations of extremism)
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Uyghur customary practices / Islamic religious practices
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Authorities have banned Islamic-sounding names, restricted fasting during Ramadan, confiscated religious materials, and regulated mosque activities [citation:12]. The regulations blur the line between lawful religious practice and 'extremism,' allowing authorities to criminalize cultural and religious expression. Two-faced people' (those deemed insufficiently supportive of state policies) face detention.
documented_statutory_conflicts.citation: UK Home Office CPIN; Human Rights Watch

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: Labor laws and state economic policies
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Uyghur land rights and customary land use
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Uyghur populations are assigned to work in factories under surveillance; the 'smart factory' system uses data from checkpoints and smartphones to hold people in place, facilitating a system of unfree labor [citation:4]. Former detainees are released to ongoing surveillance and work restrictions.
documented_statutory_conflicts.citation: Darren Byler interview; Human Rights Watch

official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.numbers_or_incidents: Chinese authorities claim to have 'wiped out 1,588 violent terrorist gangs and captured 12,995 people' and investigated 4,858 instances of illegal religious activities involving 30,645 people [citation:13]
Estimated 900,000 to 1.5 million people detained; 52 gigabytes of leaked data from Urumqi Public Security Bureau documenting arrests, surveillance, and detention [citation:4]

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Chinese government states these measures are necessary to combat the 'three forces' (separatism, extremism, terrorism) and protect the rights of all ethnic groups in Xinjiang [citation:5][citation:13]
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Uyghur rights organizations characterize these measures as systemic repression, cultural genocide, and forced assimilation targeting Uyghur identity, language, and religion [citation:4][citation:12]

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Chinese authorities describe VETCs as schools providing language, legal, and vocational education to prevent radicalization [citation:1][citation:6]
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Uyghur rights organizations characterize VETCs as high-tech prisons where Uyghurs are subjected to forced labor, political re-education, and cultural erasure; many detainees remain unaccounted for [citation:4][citation:12]

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: Surveillance System (IJOP, facial recognition, biometric collection)
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Data collection for public security and counter-terrorism purposes
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: A system of 'dataveillance' that tracks Uyghurs' every move, including private communications, social relationships, and daily routines; flags lawful behavior as 'suspicious' and triggers detention [citation:4][citation:9][citation:12]

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Chinese authorities state that all workers are protected by labor laws and have freedom to choose employment [citation:6][citation:14]
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Uyghurs are assigned to work in factories and agricultural operations under surveillance; the 'smart factory' system and checkpoints hold people in place; resources (oil, cotton) are transferred to inland provinces [citation:4][citation:11]
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.citation: Darren Byler interview; Appiah et al., 2014
